name: Tree
purpose: A recursive disclosure list: nested nodes that open and close, one selectable at a time, depth carried by an indentation ladder and by aria-level. The shape for anything genuinely hierarchical — a corporate account structure, a category picker, a document tree — where a flat list would lose the containment relation. Built #210 wave 4 (heavy seven). PROPOSED, NOT RULED; every domain semantic is Dave's (the Kpi-tile precedent, s182-D2).

props.name: nodes
props.$note: Recursive: each node is a label, an optional child list and an optional count. A node with a child list is a BRANCH and carries aria-expanded; a node without one is a LEAF.

props.name: selected
props.$note: Single selection. Multi-select with checkboxes is NOT drawn — it would compose Selection-controls and it changes the aria contract (aria-multiselectable). Receipt Q11.

props.name: expanded
props.$note: Which branches are open. Nothing is auto-expanded by the component.

props.name: lazy
props.$note: A branch whose children are fetched on first open. While fetching, the node carries aria-busy and its group shows skeleton bones.

variants.name: single-select
variants.use: The drawn component: one selected node, aria-selected, a mono leading bar.

variants.name: lazy branch
variants.use: Children arrive after the open. Drawn live rather than mocked so the loading state is real.

$states: empty tree (Empty-state, not a tree with no rows)
$consumes: Sidebar-nav (row anatomy and the collapsible-group idiom — but Sidebar-nav nests exactly one level and hard-codes its child indent; a tree cannot)
Skeleton-loader (the .bone loading rows, with its reduced-motion behaviour)

dimensions.twisty: 24x24 visual inside a 44px row, so its pointer area is 24x44 (clears 2.5.8's 24x24)
dimensions.indentLadder: 8 / 32 / 56 / 80 / 104px — a 24px step, exactly the twisty's width, so each level's twisty sits under the level above's label. Level 5 is the FLOOR; deeper nodes keep level 5's indent.
dimensions.width: NONE — width is the container's (#210 discipline). No max-width is declared on .tr or .tr-panel.

tokens.surface: tertiary/background/default on a 1px border/subtle box, border-radius/surface
tokens.selection: tertiary/background/hover surface + a 3px leading bar in form/border/active (MONO) + aria-selected
tokens.viewOnly: FULL INK, no hover surface, aria-disabled, and the words 'View only' in a .tr-meta. ⛔ NOT dimmed — the first draft used --alpha-40 and MEASURED 2.52:1 light / 3.79:1 dark in Chromium with every gate green. A view-only node is content you may READ but not ACT on; dimming it to unreadability is the #209 cancelled-mandate class exactly. A CATEGORY correction, not a colour tweak.
tokens.loading: Skeleton-loader's bone on tertiary/background/hover, shimmer suppressed under reduced-motion
tokens.focus: focus/ring, 2px, inset by -2px so it survives a flush row

behaviour.fallback: Every branch renders in the open or closed state the markup authors (collapsed groups hidden by CSS); no keyboard model, no expand or collapse on click, no lazy load.

$note.keyboard: ONE tab stop for the whole tree (roving tabindex). Down and up move through everything currently visible; right expands a closed branch or steps into an open one; left collapses an open branch or steps out to its parent; Home and End go to the first and last visible node; Enter and Space select; the asterisk key expands every branch at the focused level; a letter key jumps to the next visible node whose label starts with it, wrapping.
$note.pointer: Clicking the twisty toggles the branch. Clicking anywhere else on the row selects the node. The twisty is aria-hidden decoration, not a second control — keyboard users never need it.
$note.visibility: 'Visible' is computed as offsetParent !== null, which is exactly the question 'is any ancestor collapsed', rather than a parallel model that can drift from the DOM.
$note.lazy: First open sets aria-busy, swaps the group for skeleton bones, and replaces them with real treeitems when the children arrive. The bones are role=none so they never enter the tree's item set.

behaviour.$fallbackRender: PROVEN by JS-off render #245 (2026-09-03): 5/5 named assertions held, JavaScript disabled at the context, page.goto(file://) — notes/_subreports/assets/2026-09-03-245-L2-populate/jsoff-render.json · jsoff-tree-{before,after}.png

accessibility.structure: role=tree on the list, role=treeitem on each <li>, role=group on each nested <ul>. Every item carries aria-level, aria-setsize and aria-posinset, so depth and position are never carried by indentation alone. Non-item rows (loading bones, the empty-branch note) carry role=none so they cannot be mistaken for nodes.
accessibility.states: aria-expanded on branches only (its absence is what makes a node a leaf); aria-selected on every item; aria-busy while children load; aria-disabled on view-only nodes.
accessibility.focus: Roving tabindex — exactly one item has tabindex=0 at any moment, so a 400-node tree is one tab stop and not four hundred. The ring is drawn on the row and inset by -2px so a flush row does not clip it.
accessibility.live: Selection is echoed through a polite live region on the demo page. The component itself does not announce — selection is a state, not an event.
accessibility.targets: The twisty's pointer area is 24 wide by the full 44px row height. Measured in a real browser, not asserted; figures in the #210 lane-A receipt.
accessibility.$gate-note: ⛔ THE SNIPPET FAILS _validate_a11y.py AND IT IS DECLARED, NOT HIDDEN. The gate's role vocabulary in _a11y_target.py contains neither `tree` nor `treeitem`, and the gate is built to fail loud on an unknown role rather than let it default to 'not a control'. No native HTML element maps to treeitem, so unlike a table-backed grid these roles cannot simply be dropped. Classifying them extends a shared gate and is a RULING — not this lane's, whose fence is new files only. The recommended classification (treeitem interactive, tree non-interactive) and the browser-measured hit targets the gate would otherwise have produced are both in the #210 lane-A receipt.

antiPatterns: Making the twisty a separate <button>. That doubles the tab stops and the AT nodes; APG's treeitem is one element and expansion belongs on the arrow keys.
Giving every node its own tab stop. One roving stop, always — otherwise a deep tree is a keyboard trap in practice if not in law.
Carrying depth by indentation alone. aria-level is not optional here.
Letting the indent ladder run without a floor — level 5 is the floor; deeper nodes stop marching right rather than pushing the label off the edge.
Using text/disabled for a view-only node. It is not a disabled control, it is a node you may look at (the #209 cancelled-mandate class).
Drawing an empty TREE as a tree with no rows. An empty tree is Empty-state: there is no hierarchy and nothing for the roving stop to rove over.
Letting loading bones or the empty-branch note carry role=treeitem — they would join the item set and the arrow keys would land on them.
Distinguishing branch from leaf by a folder glyph. No folder glyph exists in the library, and the twisty plus aria-expanded already carry it.

responsive.rule: Rows are flex and the label ellipses; the indent ladder is fixed, so a narrow container narrows the LABEL, never the structure. No component-level breakpoint — only the demo page has one, at 480px, for its own chrome.
responsive.verified: Driven in headless Chromium at 1180px with 400px and 280px containers; figures in the #210 lane-A receipt.

tokenValidation.against: current store (values are Sidebar-nav's and Skeleton-loader's, unchanged)
tokenValidation.result: PASS — no token minted, no colour invented. Row chrome = Sidebar-nav's tertiary/* and form/background/pressed set; the bone = Skeleton-loader's; the selection bar = form/border/active, MONO.
tokenValidation.$note: ⚠ DECLARED, NOT SETTLED: Sidebar-nav marks CURRENT LOCATION with the same 3px bar shape in primary/border/default (#DB0011). This lane drew selection MONO rather than reuse the red, because 'the node I selected' and 'the page I am on' are different meanings and whether they share a mark is Dave's. Nothing is asserted by the mono choice — receipt Q9.

provenance.$note: #210 wave 4, lane A, from the heavy-seven fan-out brief (notes/_briefs/2026-08-20-210-wave4-heavy7-fanout-brief-v1.md). Premise re-probed in-lane: `ls knowledge/snippets/ | grep -icE '^Tree\.'` returned 0 and `grep -rli 'role="tree"' knowledge/snippets/` returned nothing. Row anatomy and the disclosure idiom come from the Sidebar-nav snippet; the loading rows from Skeleton-loader; the empty tree from Empty-state. No Figma node bound. PROPOSED, never promoted — no registration of any kind was taken by this lane.

$relationship-to-cascader-and-sidebar-na: PROPOSED, NOT ADJUDICATED. Sidebar-nav nests one level and is a NAVIGATION landmark — following a link changes the page. A tree SELECTS a node inside a page and recurses without limit. Cascader (built in the same wave, lane B) walks the same hierarchy as a SELECTION CONTROL that returns a path and closes; the overlap between the three is real and adjudicating it is Dave's, the sidebar-nav precedent.
$icon-gap: No folder / hierarchy / container glyph exists in the library. Probe, run at build: `ls knowledge/assets/icons/*/ | grep -iE "folder|hierarch|org|structure|node|group"` returns only structured-notes.svg and structured-notes-active.svg, which mean a financial product, not a container. Branch and leaf are told apart by the twisty and by aria-expanded. An _ICON-GAPS.md entry may be owed — that file is the conductor's.
$twisty-idiom-collision: Two twisty idioms now exist in the corpus and this lane did not pick between them: Sidebar-nav rotates chevron-down.svg by 180 degrees; Tree rotates chevron-right.svg by 90 degrees (the near-universal disclosure-triangle idiom). Both use real library glyphs. Dave's — receipt Q10.
